citation: Moscona, Sastry (2023). Does Directed Innovation Mitigate Climate Damage? Evidence from U.S. Agriculture. Quarterly Journal of Economics.

citation: Liu, Shamdasani, Taraz (2023). Climate Change and Labor Reallocation: Evidence from Six Decades of the Indian Census. American Economic Journal: Economic Policy.
notes: Data type mismatch (added mechanism): identifiers stored as strings broke a merge step so the build code did not run as shipped; fixed by converting to numeric.

notes: Several raw sources could not be verified (Dropbox-only files, data hand-coded from a 200-page PDF without instructions, format mismatches), and 1971 migration data the authors called unavailable exist in census PDFs. citation: Gottman JM, Coan J, Carrere S, Swanson C (1998). Predicting marital happiness and stability from newlywed interactions. Journal of Marriage and the Family.
source: Heyman & Slep (2001), J Marriage Fam (listed by Kapoor & Narayanan, family relations)
notes: Subtype: no test set; divorce-prediction accuracy was estimated on the same couples the model was fit to. Heyman & Slep showed on archival data that such accuracy collapses under cross-validation but did not rerun this study, so its own inflation is unquantified.

citation: Ye C, Fu T, Hao S, et al. (2018). Prediction of incident hypertension within the next year: prospective study using statewide electronic health records and machine learning. J Med Internet Res.
source: Chiavegatto Filho et al. (2021), comment in J Med Internet Res
notes: Subtype: illegitimate features; five of the six most important predictors were antihypertensive drugs, which signal existing hypertension, behind the reported AUC of 0.87. No corrected AUC was reported and the original authors did not reply. (First medicine source, Bouwmeester et al. 2012, names no paper.)

citation: Palazzo S, Spampinato C, Kavasidis I, Giordano D, Schmidt J, Shah M (2021). Decoding brain representations by multimodal learning of neural activity and visual features. IEEE TPAMI.
source: Ahmed, Wilbur, Bharadwaj, Siskind (2022), comment in IEEE TPAMI
notes: Subtype: non-independence; the EEG data were recorded in blocks by class, so test trials share a block (and its temporal drift) with training trials and models can classify block rather than stimulus. The comment argues the new model does not remedy this previously reported confound, and the group's randomized-trial data give near-chance accuracy.

citation: Naseriparsa M, Kashani MMR (2013). Combination of PCA with SMOTE resampling to boost the prediction rate in lung cancer dataset. Int J Computer Applications.
notes: Subtype: preprocessing on train and test together; SMOTE oversampling was applied to the whole dataset before cross-validation, so synthetic copies of test cases sit in training folds. Blagus & Lusa call the reported gain likely overoptimistic but give no corrected figure.

citation: Wall DP, Kosmicki J, DeLuca TF, Harstad E, Fusaro VA (2012). Use of machine learning to shorten observation-based screening and diagnosis of autism. Translational Psychiatry.
source: Bone et al. (2015), J Autism Dev Disord
notes: Subtypes: sampling bias and non-independence; training had 612 autism vs 11 non-spectrum cases, validation had no negatives, and 'simulated controls' were resampled from the training controls. Reported 100% accuracy fell to 83-94% unweighted recall in larger, more balanced data, and the selected items did not generalize.

citation: Luechtefeld T, Marsh D, Rowlands C, Hartung T (2018). Machine learning of toxicological big data enables read-across structure activity relationships (RASAR) outperforming animal test reproducibility. Toxicological Sciences.
source: Alves et al. (2019), letter in Toxicological Sciences
notes: Duplicate compounds acknowledged in the database without described curation, risking the same chemical in training and test sets (duplicates across splits, a leakage subtype). The letter raises the risk and asks for clarification; no corrected performance is reported.

citation: Dundar T, Ince T (2019). Sparse representation-based hyperspectral image classification using multiscale superpixels and guided filter. IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters.
notes: Subtype: non-independence; random pixel train/test splits from one scene, with features drawn from spatial neighborhoods that overlap test pixels. First entry in Nalepa et al.'s table of randomly validated methods; they did not rerun this one, but for a CNN they reran, overall accuracy dropped by 20% or more under non-overlapping splits.

citation: Kiran Kumar GR, Ramasubba Reddy M (2019). Designing a sum of squared correlations framework for enhancing SSVEP-based BCIs. IEEE TNSRE.
source: Nakanishi et al. (2020), comment in IEEE TNSRE
notes: Subtype: train/test contamination inferred; a reimplementation from the paper's description gave significantly lower accuracy under cross-validation, and simulating train-test leakage reproduced the reported accuracy, undermining the claimed superiority over TRCA. A correction notice to the original (doi 10.1109/TNSRE.2020.2974271) exists; its content wasn't checked.

citation: Coudray N, Ocampo PS, Sakellaropoulos T, et al. (2018). Classification and mutation prediction from non-small cell lung cancer histopathology images using deep learning. Nature Medicine.
notes: Subtype: non-independence; data split at slide level, so slides from the same patient appear in training and test. Rerunning the code with patient-level splits gave a significant drop in test performance; the exact magnitude was not confirmed from accessible text.

citation: Sun Z, Zhang Q, Hu W, et al. (2020). A benchmarking study of embedding-based entity alignment for knowledge graphs (OpenEA). Proceedings of the VLDB Endowment.
notes: Subtype: illegitimate feature; when no name attribute was found, the published code fell back to the last part of the entity URI as its label, which leaks ground truth for DBpedia-YAGO pairs. Berrendorf et al. also flag hyperparameters likely tuned on test sets across the field (a 13.5-point gap on one dataset); effect on OpenEA's rankings is not quantified.

citation: Arp D, Spreitzenbarth M, Hubner M, Gascon H, Rieck K (2014). Drebin: Effective and explainable detection of Android malware in your pocket. NDSS.
source: Arp et al. (2022), Dos and Don'ts of Machine Learning in Computer Security, USENIX Security
notes: Subtype: sampling bias; benign apps mostly from Google Play and malware mostly from Chinese markets, so classifiers partly learn app origin (play.google.com URL is a top benign feature). Recall fell by more than 10 points when malware came only from Google Play; same first author as the original.

citation: Li J, Gao H, Ye Z, Deng J, Ouyang D (2022). In silico formulation prediction of drug/cyclodextrin/polymer ternary complexes by machine learning and molecular modeling techniques. Carbohydrate Polymers.
source: Murray et al. (2023), Eur J Pharm Sci
notes: Subtype: feature selection on train and test together; model inputs were chosen using all data rather than training data only. Murray et al. identify this from the methods description; no corrected performance is given.

citation: Muchlinski D, Siroky D, He J, Kocher M (2016). Comparing random forest with logistic regression for predicting class-imbalanced civil war onset data. Political Analysis.
source: Kapoor & Narayanan (2023), Patterns, civil war case study
notes: Subtype: preprocessing on train and test together; training and test data were imputed jointly with rfImpute, with the outcome in the imputation model. Corrected, random forest AUC fell from 0.94 to 0.64, no better than logistic regression (0.54-0.68), so the superiority claim fails.

citation: Muchlinski D, Siroky D, He J, Kocher M (2016). Comparing random forest with logistic regression for predicting class-imbalanced civil war onset data. Political Analysis.
notes: In the released imputed dataset, 777 rows whose civil war onset is missing in the source data (Hegre & Sambanis) carry a value of peace. The imputation code was not shared, so how this happened can't be checked; the error propagated to papers reusing the dataset.

citation: Colaresi M, Mahmood Z (2017). Do the robot: Lessons from machine learning to improve conflict forecasting. Journal of Peace Research.
source: Kapoor & Narayanan (2023), Patterns, civil war case study
notes: Subtype: preprocessing on train and test together, inherited by reusing Muchlinski et al.'s jointly imputed dataset and splitting it. Corrected, their random forest AUC fell from 0.91 to 0.75, below Fearon & Laitin's logistic regression (0.79).

citation: Wang Y (2019). Comparing random forest with logistic regression for predicting class-imbalanced civil war onset data: a comment. Political Analysis.
source: Kapoor & Narayanan (2023), Patterns, civil war case study
notes: Subtype: preprocessing on train and test together, from reusing the jointly imputed dataset. With within-fold imputation the boosted models' AUC fell from 0.94 to about 0.82 vs 0.77 for logistic regression, shrinking but not removing the advantage.

citation: Wang Y (2019). Comparing random forest with logistic regression for predicting class-imbalanced civil war onset data: a comment. Political Analysis.
source: Kapoor & Narayanan (2023), Patterns, civil war case study
notes: Subtype: temporal leakage; shuffled k-fold cross-validation on time-ordered country-year data. With a temporal split (train before 1988) logistic regression matched or beat AdaBoost and gradient boosting (0.78 vs 0.77/0.75), so the AUC gap of 0.14 vanished.

citation: Kaufman AR, Kraft P, Sen M (2019). Improving Supreme Court forecasting using boosted decision trees. Political Analysis.
notes: Subtype: illegitimate features; the civil war application used variables affected by or proxying the outcome (e.g., population and polity score unlagged, onset-coded variables). After correction, AdaBoost and logistic regression were about equal and neither beat a previous-year baseline; the Supreme Court application was not examined.

citation: Kaufman AR, Kraft P, Sen M (2019). Improving Supreme Court forecasting using boosted decision trees. Political Analysis.
notes: Mechanism: mis-set Lasso penalty selection made the Lasso comparison model always predict peace, alongside a weak always-peace baseline, which flattered AdaBoost by comparison. Kapoor & Narayanan attribute most of the performance gap to leakage instead.

citation: Kaufman AR, Kraft P, Sen M (2019). Improving Supreme Court forecasting using boosted decision trees. Political Analysis.
notes: Missing values were replaced with zeros, making missing indistinguishable from a true zero. Re-imputing properly did not change results.
